content.title: About
content.content: Green peas are the edible seeds of the pea plant (Pisum sativum) harvested at full maturity and boiled. They have a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a tender yet slightly crisp texture. Peas are commonly served as a side dish, and used in salads, soups, and purees.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green peas are a good source of plant protein.
They are cultivated in temperate regions worldwide.
Peas belong to the legume family, which can fix nitrogen in the soil.
Ancient cultures used peas both as food and medicine.
There are many varieties differing in pod size and seed color.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: One cup of cooked peas provides about 8 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Dietary fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Peas contain folate, thiamine, and vitamin B6, important for metabolism.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: They provide iron, magnesium, phosphorus, and potassium, supporting heart and nerve function.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Peas raise blood sugar slowly, which is beneficial for glucose control.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to legumes.

items.title: Gas production
items.content: Legumes can cause flatulence in sensitive people.

items.title: Purine content
items.content: Large amounts may increase uric acid levels in people prone to gout.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Peas can be enjoyed as a standalone side, added to salads, soups, stews, mashed into puree, or incorporated into vegetable casseroles. They pair well with mint, lemon, garlic, and olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked peas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Frozen peas retain quality for up to 6 months.
